For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ have a finite Kraus representation
$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger$. Then $\Phi$ is completely positive.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

For $A\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and $B\in M_{n\times m}(F)$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA).$$

The two products may have different sizes, and the equality includes $m=0$ or
$n=0$.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces. A
**quantum channel** from $H$ to $K$ is a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ ([[def-linear-map]]) that is completely
positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and trace-preserving, meaning

$$\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where trace is the basis-independent trace of a finite-dimensional
endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]). Trace preservation is
required on the full operator space, not only on density operators. This
definition is mathematical and assumes no physical realization.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

derivations.claim: Let $e$ and $f$ range over an orthonormal product basis of $H_T\otimes H_E$. For input basis vector $|j\rangle\otimes e$ and output basis vector $|r,s\rangle\otimes f$, the definition and orthonormality [F1] give $\langle L_k(|j\rangle\otimes e),|r,s\rangle\otimes f\rangle=\langle e,f\rangle$ if $j=r=s=k$, and $0$ otherwise. By the defining adjoint identity [F6] and the fact that these product vectors form bases, $L_k^\dagger(|r,s\rangle\otimes f)=|k\rangle\otimes f$ when $r=s=k$, and is $0$ otherwise. Hence $L_k^\dagger L_k(|j\rangle\otimes e)=|j\rangle\otimes e$ when $j=k$ and $0$ otherwise. Summing over $k$ proves $\sum_{k\in\mathsf K}L_k^\dagger L_k=I_{ATE}$ on a basis, so it holds on the full input space.

The formula in the Statement is a finite Kraus sum, so [F2] makes $\mathcal C$ completely positive. For every operator $X$, trace linearity [F3] and cyclicity [F4] give $\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal C(X))=\sum_k\operatorname{tr}(XL_k^\dagger L_k)=\operatorname{tr}(X\sum_kL_k^\dagger L_k)=\operatorname{tr}(X)$ by step 1.1. These are precisely the channel conditions [F5].

For $\xi_{ATE}=\sum_j|j\rangle\langle j|\otimes\xi^j_{TE}$, the basis action gives $L_k\xi_{ATE}L_k^\dagger=|k,k\rangle\langle k,k|\otimes\xi^k_{TE}$; all other input-key blocks are annihilated by $L_k$. Summing over $k$ yields the stated copy formula.

be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

For every linear map $A:H\to K$ ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces,

$$\|A\|_1=\operatorname{tr}_H\!\left(\sqrt{A^*A}\right).$$

Here $A^*A$ and its non-negative square root are endomorphisms of the domain
$H$; the trace is taken on $H$.

$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the

The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be an endomorphism. The endomorphism $T$ is **self-adjoint** when

$$T^*=T,$$

and **normal** when

$$TT^*=T^*T,$$

where $T^*$ is the adjoint from
[[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]].

Every self-adjoint endomorphism is normal, because $TT^*=T^2=T^*T$.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, with **conjugation** $z\mapsto\overline z$
the identity on $\mathbb R$ and complex conjugation on $\mathbb C$
([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]). A **real** or
**complex inner-product space** is an $\mathbb F$-vector space $V$ together with
an inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:V\times V\to\mathbb F$ in the sense
of [[def-inner-product-space]]: for all $u,v,w\in V$ and $a,b\in\mathbb F$,

$$\langle au+bv,w\rangle=a\langle u,w\rangle+b\langle v,w\rangle,\qquad \langle u,v\rangle=\overline{\langle v,u\rangle},\qquad \langle v,v\rangle\ge0,\quad \langle v,v\rangle=0\iff v=0 .$$

**Conjugate-linearity in the second argument.** Conjugate symmetry together with
linearity in the first argument gives, for all $w\in V$,

$$\langle w,au+bv\rangle=\overline{\langle au+bv,w\rangle}=\overline{a\langle u,w\rangle+b\langle v,w\rangle}=\overline a\,\langle w,u\rangle+\overline b\,\langle w,v\rangle .$$

**Induced length.** The **induced length**, or inner-product norm, of $v$ is

$$\|v\|:=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle},$$

which is exactly the published [[def-inner-product-norm]]: positive definiteness
makes $\langle v,v\rangle$ a nonnegative real with a unique nonnegative square
root, so that $\|v\|\ge0$, $\|v\|=0$ exactly for $v=0$, and
$\langle v,v\rangle=\|v\|^2$.

**The convention on this page.** Every inner-product space below is real or
complex in this sense, the pairing is linear in the first argument and
conjugate-linear in the second, and $\|v\|$ always denotes the induced length.
In the real case conjugation is the identity and $|z|$ is the absolute value of
$\mathbb R$; in the complex case they are complex conjugation and the complex
modulus. All statements below are therefore written once and read in either
scalar field.

derivations.claim: Each $X_i$ is normal because $X_i^\dagger=X_i$, so $X_iX_i^\dagger=X_i^\dagger X_i$; apply [F1] to choose an orthonormal eigenbasis $(e_{i,j})_j$ with $X_ie_{i,j}=\lambda_{i,j}e_{i,j}$ and $\lambda_{i,j}\in\mathbb C$. Since the inner product is linear in its first argument and $\langle e_{i,j},e_{i,j}\rangle=1$, the expectation equals $\lambda_{i,j}$; hence $\lambda_{i,j}\in\mathbb R$. By [F3], the vectors $|i\rangle\otimes e_{i,j}$ over all $i,j$ form an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb C^I\otimes H_E$. Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

Let $\mathsf K$ be a finite nonempty key alphabet with a fixed ordering, and let $H_T,H_E$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with $H_T\ne\{0\}$ and $H_E\ne\{0\}$. Give the key register $H_A=\mathbb C^{\mathsf K}$ its corresponding computational basis $(|k\rangle)_{k\in\mathsf K}$. For each $k\in\mathsf K$, define $L_k:H_A\otimes H_T\otimes H_E\to H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_T\otimes H_E$ by

$$L_k(|j\rangle\otimes x)=\begin{cases}|k,k\rangle\otimes x,&j=k,\\0,&j\ne k,\end{cases}$$

and extend linearly, where $H_B$ is another copy of $H_A$. Then

$$\mathcal C(X):=\sum_{k\in\mathsf K}L_kXL_k^\dagger$$

is a finite-dimensional quantum channel. On every input classical in $A$, $\xi_{ATE}=\sum_k|k\rangle\langle k|\otimes\xi^k_{TE}$, it acts by

$$\mathcal C(\xi_{ATE})=\sum_{k\in\mathsf K}|k,k\rangle\langle k,k|\otimes\xi^k_{TE}.$$

This map copies a measured classical key register; it does not copy arbitrary quantum states.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces. A
**quantum channel** from $H$ to $K$ is a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ ([[def-linear-map]]) that is completely
positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and trace-preserving, meaning

$$\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where trace is the basis-independent trace of a finite-dimensional
endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]). Trace preservation is
required on the full operator space, not only on density operators. This
definition is mathematical and assumes no physical realization.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and write $\mathcal L(H)$ and $\mathcal L(K)$ for their vector spaces of complex-linear endomorphisms with pointwise operations ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]], [[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]], [[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]]). Let $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be complex-linear. For each integer $r\ge1$, put $R=\mathbb C^r$ with its standard ordered register basis ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). Write an operator $X\in\mathcal L(H\otimes R)$ in its unique $r\times r$ block form $X=[X_{ij}]$ with $X_{ij}\in\mathcal L(H)$, and define $\Phi^{(r)}(X)$ to have blocks $[\Phi(X_{ij})]$ on $K\otimes R$. Lemma [[lem-qc-finite-ancilla-amplification-is-block-map]] proves that this block rule defines a linear map on the full operator space for every finite $r$. For $r=1$, the extension is $\Phi$ under the canonical unitary identifications $x\mapsto x\otimes e_0$ and $y\mapsto y\otimes e_0$ proved in that lemma.

The map $\Phi$ is **completely positive** if, for every finite $r\ge1$, $\Phi^{(r)}$ sends every nonnegative operator on $H\otimes R$ to a nonnegative operator on $K\otimes R$ ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]). The quantifier includes $r=1$; complete positivity therefore implies positivity. No Kraus, Choi, or Stinespring characterization is part of this definition.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on $H$ (nonnegative operators of trace one; [[def-qc-density-operator]]). Their **trace distance** is
$$D(\rho,\sigma):=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1,$$
where $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the trace norm ([[def-qc-trace-norm]]). The factor $1/2$ is part of this state-distance convention. The diamond norm below is an unhalved norm on maps.

Let $I$ be a finite nonempty set with a fixed ordering, let $H_E$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and let $X_i:H_E\to H_E$ be self-adjoint for each $i\in I$. On the ordered register $\mathbb C^I\otimes H_E$ with the corresponding computational basis, set $X=\sum_{i\in I}|i\rangle\langle i|\otimes X_i$. Then

$$\|X\|_1=\sum_{i\in I}\|X_i\|_1.$$

Let $A:H\to K$ be a linear map ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional complex
inner-product spaces. If $U:K\to K$ and $V:H\to H$ are unitary, then
$\|UAV\|_1=\|A\|_1$. If $P:H\to H$ is non-negative (positive semidefinite),
then

$$\|P\|_1=\operatorname{tr}_H(P).$$

Here non-negative means self-adjoint with
$\langle Pv,v\rangle\ge0$ for all $v$, as in
[[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]].

Let $A:H\to K$ be a linear map ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional complex
inner-product spaces. Then

$$\|A\|_1=\max\{\,|\operatorname{tr}_H(B^*A)|: B:H\to K\text{ linear and }\|B\|\le1\,\}.$$

Consequently, on the vector space of linear maps $H\to K$, the trace norm is
nonnegative, absolutely homogeneous, definite, and satisfies the triangle
inequality.

derivations.claim: The blocks of $\rho_{ATE}$ are the finite sums $\sum_bR_E^{a,b,t}$, so they are nonnegative. Their traces sum to the trace of $\rho_{ABTE}$ by [F1], hence to one; therefore $\rho_{ATE}$ is a density operator. Complete positivity and trace preservation [F2] show that $\gamma_{ABTE}=\mathcal C(\rho_{ATE})$ is also a density operator, as required for [F3].

By [F2], $\gamma_{ABTE}$ has block $\sum_bR_E^{a,b,t}$ in each key-diagonal slot $(a,a,t)$ and zero in every slot $(a,b,t)$ with $b
e a$. Thus $ho_{ABTE}-\gamma_{ABTE}$ has block $R_E^{a,b,t}$ in each slot with $a
e b$, block $-\sum_{b
e a}R_E^{a,b,t}$ in slot $(a,a,t)$, and zero elsewhere. Each displayed nonzero block is self-adjoint because it is a positive block or its negative.

Apply [F4] to these orthogonal classical blocks. For $a
e b$, [F5] gives $\|R_E^{a,b,t}\|_1=\operatorname{tr}(R_E^{a,b,t})$. The sum $\sum_{b
e a}R_E^{a,b,t}$ is nonnegative, so [F5] and [F6] give $\|-\sum_{b
e a}R_E^{a,b,t}\|_1=\sum_{b
e a}\operatorname{tr}(R_E^{a,b,t})$. Therefore $\|ho_{ABTE}-\gamma_{ABTE}\|_1=2\sum_{a

Fix finite nonempty sets $\mathsf K$ and $\mathsf T$ of key values and public transcripts, respectively, and fix an ordering of each finite set. Choose a symbol $\bot\notin\mathsf K$ and order $\mathsf K\cup\{\bot\}$ by placing $\bot$ after the ordered keys. The full key registers $A$ and $B$ are copies of $Q_{|\mathsf K|+1}$, with computational basis labelled by $\mathsf K\cup\{\bot\}$; the transcript register $T$ is $Q_{|\mathsf T|}$, with basis labelled by $\mathsf T$, using [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]. For accepted-state calculations, identify the subspaces spanned by the key vectors $|a\rangle$, $a\in\mathsf K$, with $Q_{|\mathsf K|}$; operators on these subspaces are embedded in the full key registers by zero extension. A **finite two-party key-distribution protocol** is a finite-round interaction of Alice and Bob in which each quantum register is nonzero and finite-dimensional, every local quantum operation is a quantum channel or finite instrument ([[def-qc-quantum-channel]], [[def-qc-instrument-and-conditional-state]]), and every classical message alphabet is finite. Eve's operation on each insecure quantum transmission is a channel from the sent register and her current memory to the received register and her updated memory. The parties communicate through an ideal authenticated public channel: each message is delivered unchanged to its intended honest recipient, and Eve receives a copy. The transcript $t\in\mathsf T$ records all such messages, including messages that lead the protocol to abort. This is an assumption about the communication resource; it does not prove security of an authentication implementation. Any implementation error must be included in the abort convention or in an additional security parameter.

For each allowed adversarial strategy, the final output is a normalized state, classical in the key registers $A,B$ and transcript register $T$, on $A\otimes B\otimes T\otimes E$, where $E$ is Eve's retained finite-dimensional quantum system. Both honest parties output the common abort symbol $\bot$ on an abort. In the ordered product basis this state has the form

$$\rho_{ABTE}=\sum_{t\in\mathsf T}|\bot,\bot,t\rangle\langle\bot,\bot,t|\otimes\omega_E^{\bot,t}+\sum_{a,b\in\mathsf K,\ t\in\mathsf T}|a,b,t\rangle\langle a,b,t|\otimes\omega_E^{a,b,t},$$

where every block $\omega_E^{\bot,t}$ and $\omega_E^{a,b,t}$ is nonnegative and the sum of their traces is $1$. The trace of each block is the joint probability of its displayed classical labels. All registers and tensor factors retain the displayed order. The transcript is included separately from $E$ so that secrecy below explicitly conditions on the public messages as well as Eve's quantum information.

Fix one adversarial strategy in a protocol from [[def-qkd-finite-authenticated-protocol]]. Write its final output blocks as $\omega_E^{\bot,t}$ on abort and $\omega_E^{a,b,t}$ on acceptance. Define the abort and accepted transcript-adversary substates by

$$\rho_{TE}^{\rm abort}:=\sum_{t\in\mathsf T}|t\rangle\langle t|\otimes\omega_E^{\bot,t},\qquad \rho_{TE}^{\rm acc}:=\sum_{t\in\mathsf T}|t\rangle\langle t|\otimes\sum_{a,b\in\mathsf K}\omega_E^{a,b,t}.$$

The accepted part of the full real state is $\rho_{ABTE}^{\rm acc}:=\sum_{a,b\in\mathsf K,\ t\in\mathsf T}|a,b,t\rangle\langle a,b,t|\otimes\omega_E^{a,b,t}$.

Their traces are $p_{\rm abort}$ and $p_{\rm acc}$, with $p_{\rm abort}+p_{\rm acc}=1$. If $p_{\rm acc}>0$, put $\rho_{ABTE}^{\top}:=\rho_{ABTE}^{\rm acc}/p_{\rm acc}$ and define the normalized accepted marginals directly from their classical blocks:

$$\rho_{ATE}^{\top}:=\sum_{a,t}|a,t\rangle\langle a,t|\otimes\frac{1}{p_{\rm acc}}\sum_b\omega_E^{a,b,t},\qquad \rho_{TE}^{\top}:=\sum_t|t\rangle\langle t|\otimes\frac{1}{p_{\rm acc}}\sum_{a,b}\omega_E^{a,b,t}.$$

For $m:=|\mathsf K|$, define the uniform key state $\tau_A:=m^{-1}\sum_{a\in\mathsf K}|a\rangle\langle a|$ and the ideal uniform shared-key state $\tau_{AB}:=m^{-1}\sum_{a\in\mathsf K}|a,a\rangle\langle a,a|$. The **abort-aware ideal full output** keeps the real abort branch and the accepted transcript-adversary marginal, but replaces the accepted keys with a uniform shared key independent of both:

$$\rho_{ABTE}^{\rm ideal}:=\sum_t|\bot,\bot,t\rangle\langle\bot,\bot,t|\otimes\omega_E^{\bot,t}+\tau_{AB}\otimes\rho_{TE}^{\rm acc}.$$

Let $\rho_{ABTE}^{\rm real}$ be the normalized output from the protocol definition. The **real-ideal trace-distance error** is $\delta_{\rm id}:=D(\rho_{ABTE}^{\rm real},\rho_{ABTE}^{\rm ideal})$, using [[def-qc-trace-distance]]. The **correctness error** is $\varepsilon_{\rm cor}:=\Pr[K_A\ne K_B]=\sum_{a\ne b,t}\operatorname{tr}(\omega_E^{a,b,t})$; the common abort output contributes no mismatch. The **secrecy error** is

$$\varepsilon_{\rm sec}:=\begin{cases}p_{\rm acc}D(\rho_{ATE}^{\top},\tau_A\otimes\rho_{TE}^{\top}),&p_{\rm acc}>0,\\0,&p_{\rm acc}=0.\end{cases}$$

This is an unconditional convention: the normalized secrecy distance on acceptance is weighted by the acceptance probability. Errors in a protocol are uniform bounds on these strategy-specific quantities over all allowed adversarial strategies.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be linear. The following are equivalent:

1. $T$ is non-negative.
2. $T$ is self-adjoint and every eigenvalue of $T$ is a nonnegative real number.
3. Some orthonormal basis makes the matrix of $T$ diagonal with nonnegative real diagonal entries.
4. There exists a linear map $S:V\to V$ such that $T=S^*S$.

derivations.claim: The real state is nonnegative because its orthogonal classical blocks are nonnegative by [F1]. Its trace is the sum of their traces by [F5], which is one by [F1], so it is a density operator by [F3]. If $p_{\rm acc}>0$, dividing each accepted block by $p_{\rm acc}$ preserves nonnegativity and makes the trace sum equal to one; hence $\rho_{ABTE}^{\top}$ is a density operator.

In the explicit sums of [F2], each $ATE$ block is $p_{\rm acc}^{-1}\sum_b\omega_E^{a,b,t}$ and each $TE$ block is $p_{\rm acc}^{-1}\sum_{a,b}\omega_E^{a,b,t}$. These are nonnegative finite sums. By [F5], their traces sum to $p_{\rm acc}^{-1}p_{\rm acc}=1$, so both marginals are density operators by [F3]. The states $\tau_A$ and $\tau_{AB}$ are diagonal with $m$ entries equal to $1/m$ and all other entries zero, so each is nonnegative with trace one. In the product register, $\tau_A\otimes\rho_{TE}^{\top}$ has one block $m^{-1}\rho_{TE}^{\top}$ per key, hence is nonnegative and has trace $m(m^{-1})=1$.

The ideal accepted blocks occur only at key pairs $(a,a)$ and equal $m^{-1}\sum_{b,c}\omega_E^{b,c,t}$ for each $a,t$; they are nonnegative and their total trace is $p_{\rm acc}$ by [F5]. Its abort blocks are the original nonnegative blocks with total trace $1-p_{\rm acc}$ by [F1]–[F2]. These lie in mutually orthogonal classical slots, so the full ideal state is nonnegative and has trace $p_{\rm acc}+1-p_{\rm acc}=1$, hence is a density operator by [F3]. If $p_{\rm acc}=0$, nonnegativity makes each accepted block's trace nonnegative; their sum is zero, so each trace is zero. By [F6], each such block has only nonnegative eigenvalues summing to zero and is therefore zero. The accepted ideal block is also zero, so the ideal output equals the real abort-only state.

$$L_k(|j\rangle\otimes x)=\begin{cases}|k,k\rangle\otimes x,&j=k,\\0,&j\ne k,\end{cases}$$

$$\mathcal C(X):=\sum_{k\in\mathsf K}L_kXL_k^\dagger$$

Fix finite nonempty sets $\mathsf K$ and $\mathsf T$ of key values and public transcripts, respectively, and fix an ordering of each finite set. Choose a symbol $\bot\notin\mathsf K$ and order $\mathsf K\cup\{\bot\}$ by placing $\bot$ after the ordered keys. The full key registers $A$ and $B$ are copies of $Q_{|\mathsf K|+1}$, with computational basis labelled by $\mathsf K\cup\{\bot\}$; the transcript register $T$ is $Q_{|\mathsf T|}$, with basis labelled by $\mathsf T$, using [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]. For accepted-state calculations, identify the subspaces spanned by the key vectors $|a\rangle$, $a\in\mathsf K$, with $Q_{|\mathsf K|}$; operators on these subspaces are embedded in the full key registers by zero extension. A **finite two-party key-distribution protocol** is a finite-round interaction of Alice and Bob in which each quantum register is nonzero and finite-dimensional, every local quantum operation is a quantum channel or finite instrument ([[def-qc-quantum-channel]], [[def-qc-instrument-and-conditional-state]]), and every classical message alphabet is finite. Eve's operation on each insecure quantum transmission is a channel from the sent register and her current memory to the received register and her updated memory. The parties communicate through an ideal authenticated public channel: each message is delivered unchanged to its intended honest recipient, and Eve receives a copy. The transcript $t\in\mathsf T$ records all such messages, including messages that lead the protocol to abort. This is an assumption about the communication resource; it does not prove security of an authentication implementation. Any implementation error must be included in the abort convention or in an additional security parameter.

For each allowed adversarial strategy, the final output is a normalized state, classical in the key registers $A,B$ and transcript register $T$, on $A\otimes B\otimes T\otimes E$, where $E$ is Eve's retained finite-dimensional quantum system. Both honest parties output the common abort symbol $\bot$ on an abort. In the ordered product basis this state has the form

$$\rho_{ABTE}=\sum_{t\in\mathsf T}|\bot,\bot,t\rangle\langle\bot,\bot,t|\otimes\omega_E^{\bot,t}+\sum_{a,b\in\mathsf K,\ t\in\mathsf T}|a,b,t\rangle\langle a,b,t|\otimes\omega_E^{a,b,t},$$

where every block $\omega_E^{\bot,t}$ and $\omega_E^{a,b,t}$ is nonnegative and the sum of their traces is $1$. The trace of each block is the joint probability of its displayed classical labels. All registers and tensor factors retain the displayed order. The transcript is included separately from $E$ so that secrecy below explicitly conditions on the public messages as well as Eve's quantum information.

Fix one adversarial strategy in a protocol from [[def-qkd-finite-authenticated-protocol]]. Write its final output blocks as $\omega_E^{\bot,t}$ on abort and $\omega_E^{a,b,t}$ on acceptance. Define the abort and accepted transcript-adversary substates by

$$\rho_{TE}^{\rm abort}:=\sum_{t\in\mathsf T}|t\rangle\langle t|\otimes\omega_E^{\bot,t},\qquad \rho_{TE}^{\rm acc}:=\sum_{t\in\mathsf T}|t\rangle\langle t|\otimes\sum_{a,b\in\mathsf K}\omega_E^{a,b,t}.$$

The accepted part of the full real state is $\rho_{ABTE}^{\rm acc}:=\sum_{a,b\in\mathsf K,\ t\in\mathsf T}|a,b,t\rangle\langle a,b,t|\otimes\omega_E^{a,b,t}$.

Their traces are $p_{\rm abort}$ and $p_{\rm acc}$, with $p_{\rm abort}+p_{\rm acc}=1$. If $p_{\rm acc}>0$, put $\rho_{ABTE}^{\top}:=\rho_{ABTE}^{\rm acc}/p_{\rm acc}$ and define the normalized accepted marginals directly from their classical blocks:

$$\rho_{ATE}^{\top}:=\sum_{a,t}|a,t\rangle\langle a,t|\otimes\frac{1}{p_{\rm acc}}\sum_b\omega_E^{a,b,t},\qquad \rho_{TE}^{\top}:=\sum_t|t\rangle\langle t|\otimes\frac{1}{p_{\rm acc}}\sum_{a,b}\omega_E^{a,b,t}.$$

For $m:=|\mathsf K|$, define the uniform key state $\tau_A:=m^{-1}\sum_{a\in\mathsf K}|a\rangle\langle a|$ and the ideal uniform shared-key state $\tau_{AB}:=m^{-1}\sum_{a\in\mathsf K}|a,a\rangle\langle a,a|$. The **abort-aware ideal full output** keeps the real abort branch and the accepted transcript-adversary marginal, but replaces the accepted keys with a uniform shared key independent of both:

$$\rho_{ABTE}^{\rm ideal}:=\sum_t|\bot,\bot,t\rangle\langle\bot,\bot,t|\otimes\omega_E^{\bot,t}+\tau_{AB}\otimes\rho_{TE}^{\rm acc}.$$

Let $\rho_{ABTE}^{\rm real}$ be the normalized output from the protocol definition. The **real-ideal trace-distance error** is $\delta_{\rm id}:=D(\rho_{ABTE}^{\rm real},\rho_{ABTE}^{\rm ideal})$, using [[def-qc-trace-distance]]. The **correctness error** is $\varepsilon_{\rm cor}:=\Pr[K_A\ne K_B]=\sum_{a\ne b,t}\operatorname{tr}(\omega_E^{a,b,t})$; the common abort output contributes no mismatch. The **secrecy error** is

$$\varepsilon_{\rm sec}:=\begin{cases}p_{\rm acc}D(\rho_{ATE}^{\top},\tau_A\otimes\rho_{TE}^{\top}),&p_{\rm acc}>0,\\0,&p_{\rm acc}=0.\end{cases}$$

This is an unconditional convention: the normalized secrecy distance on acceptance is weighted by the acceptance probability. Errors in a protocol are uniform bounds on these strategy-specific quantities over all allowed adversarial strategies.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on $H$ (nonnegative operators of trace one; [[def-qc-density-operator]]). Their **trace distance** is
$$D(\rho,\sigma):=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1,$$
where $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the trace norm ([[def-qc-trace-norm]]). The factor $1/2$ is part of this state-distance convention. The diamond norm below is an unhalved norm on maps.

For every linear map $A:H\to K$ ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces,

$$\|A\|_1=\operatorname{tr}_H\!\left(\sqrt{A^*A}\right).$$

Here $A^*A$ and its non-negative square root are endomorphisms of the domain
$H$; the trace is taken on $H$.

Let $A:H\to K$ be a linear map ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional complex
inner-product spaces. If $U:K\to K$ and $V:H\to H$ are unitary, then
$\|UAV\|_1=\|A\|_1$. If $P:H\to H$ is non-negative (positive semidefinite),
then

$$\|P\|_1=\operatorname{tr}_H(P).$$

Here non-negative means self-adjoint with
$\langle Pv,v\rangle\ge0$ for all $v$, as in
[[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]].

For every finite authenticated key-distribution protocol and each fixed allowed adversarial strategy, let $\delta_{\rm id}$, $\varepsilon_{\rm cor}$, and $\varepsilon_{\rm sec}$ be as in [[def-qkd-abort-aware-composable-security]]. Then

$$\delta_{\rm id}\le\varepsilon_{\rm cor}+\varepsilon_{\rm sec}.$$

Consequently, if correctness and secrecy errors are bounded uniformly over all allowed adversarial strategies by $\varepsilon_{\rm cor}$ and $\varepsilon_{\rm sec}$, respectively, then the real-ideal trace distance is uniformly at most their sum.
